legacyRecords.title: extractBundle() writes entry.name through path.join(destDir, entry.name) with no normalization or ../absolute-path rejection
legacyRecords.detail: extractBundle() writes entry.name through path.join(destDir, entry.name) with no normalization or ../absolute-path rejection. It is not currently on the marketplace install path, but it is an exported helper and test fixture code already exercises extraction. Fix: Reuse normalizeArchivePath-style validation before writing, and assert the resolved target stays under destDir.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Reuse normalizeArchivePath-style validation before writing, and assert the resolved target stays under destDir.

legacyRecords.title: resolved.graph is trusted as typed JSON, and the bundle cache path is built from entry.id.replace("/", "-"), which only replaces the first slash and does not assert entry.id === defineManifest(entry.manifest).id
legacyRecords.detail: resolved.graph is trusted as typed JSON, and the bundle cache path is built from entry.id.replace("/", "-"), which only replaces the first slash and does not assert entry.id === defineManifest(entry.manifest).id. A compromised or malicious marketplace can return an id like a/b/../../../target, causing path.join() normalization to write the downloaded bundle outside the intended store directory if the process has permission. Fix: Runtime-validate resolve responses, derive the filename from the validated manifest id or a strict slug encoder, and assert the resolved id matches the manifest id before writing.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Runtime-validate resolve responses, derive the filename from the validated manifest id or a strict slug encoder, and assert the resolved id matches the manifest id before writing.

legacyRecords.title: relayos lock verify unpacks lock bundles using the CLI's legacy tar/gzip unpackBundle() and expects manifest.json inside the archive, while the current publish/install path uses packArchive() with the manifest outside the archive and computes computeManifestDigest(manifest, bundle)
legacyRecords.detail: relayos lock verify unpacks lock bundles using the CLI's legacy tar/gzip unpackBundle() and expects manifest.json inside the archive, while the current publish/install path uses packArchive() with the manifest outside the archive and computes computeManifestDigest(manifest, bundle). The verifier can fail to validate real installed marketplace bundles, weakening the local tamper-check story. Fix: Store the manifest alongside the resolved bundle in the lock/store, or verify using the same packArchive + external manifest contract as install.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Store the manifest alongside the resolved bundle in the lock/store, or verify using the same packArchive + external manifest contract as install.

legacyRecords.title: extract(digest, archive) trusts the caller-supplied digest as the content-address dir name and does NOT recompute computeManifestDigest over the bytes before extracting
legacyRecords.detail: extract(digest, archive) trusts the caller-supplied digest as the content-address dir name and does NOT recompute computeManifestDigest over the bytes before extracting. Sole caller today (SystemProfileReconciler) feeds trusted builtins, and the untrusted install path (extension-installer.ts:61) verifies digest first, so not exploitable now. But it's an unguarded primitive: a future caller wiring marketplace/third-party bundles through extract() without verifying would extract substituted bytes under the claimed digest. Zip-slip mitigated upstream (normalizeArchivePath rejects ../absolute; no symlink entries). Fix: Make extract() self-verifying: recompute computeManifestDigest(manifest, archive) and assert == digest before writing, throwing on mismatch.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Make extract() self-verifying: recompute computeManifestDigest(manifest, archive) and assert == digest before writing, throwing on mismatch.

legacyRecords.title: The provider resolves user-supplied file://, absolute, or home-relative repoPath, then spawns git with that path as cwd and returns parsed diff output
legacyRecords.detail: The provider resolves user-supplied file://, absolute, or home-relative repoPath, then spawns git with that path as cwd and returns parsed diff output. With the manifest match above, local preview rendering can read diffs from arbitrary accessible Git repositories, not just the current RelayOS workspace. Fix: Resolve and enforce an allowed root before spawning git; reject symlink escapes after realpath.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Resolve and enforce an allowed root before spawning git; reject symlink escapes after realpath.

legacyRecords.title: git diff stdout/stderr are accumulated into unbounded strings and there is no timeout
legacyRecords.detail: git diff stdout/stderr are accumulated into unbounded strings and there is no timeout. A huge diff or slow Git process can consume extension-runner memory or hang preview generation. Fix: Add a max output byte cap, pass -- where path args are ever introduced, and kill the child after a short preview timeout.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Add a max output byte cap, pass -- where path args are ever introduced, and kill the child after a short preview timeout.

legacyRecords.title: GitDiffFetcherInput accepts raw repoPath, branchRef, and optional baseRef strings with no format or length limits
legacyRecords.detail: GitDiffFetcherInput accepts raw repoPath, branchRef, and optional baseRef strings with no format or length limits. The implementation uses argv arrays, so this is not command injection, but it allows odd ref names and very large inputs to reach git and error/log paths. Fix: Validate repo path form, cap string lengths, and reject refs that start with - or contain control characters.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Validate repo path form, cap string lengths, and reject refs that start with - or contain control characters.

legacyRecords.title: readAllBytes() buffers an entire stream into memory with no byte cap
legacyRecords.detail: readAllBytes() buffers an entire stream into memory with no byte cap. It is a convenience helper, but InMemoryBlobStore.put() uses it for streamed input, so a caller that forgets an upstream limit can allocate arbitrarily large buffers. Fix: Add a capped variant or require a maxBytes argument for stream reads.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Add a capped variant or require a maxBytes argument for stream reads.

legacyRecords.title: BlobStore.put exposes expectedSize but no maxBytes option
legacyRecords.detail: BlobStore.put exposes expectedSize but no maxBytes option. Callers must remember to enforce size before or during upload; the storage primitive cannot fail closed for oversized streams. Fix: Add maxBytes to PutOptions and require implementations to stop reading/writing once exceeded.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Add maxBytes to PutOptions and require implementations to stop reading/writing once exceeded.

legacyRecords.title: allowedResolutionKindsForState is a pure advisory transition table with NO principal/role/principal-kind enforcement — the package is type/data only and enforces none of CORE_INVARIANTS
legacyRecords.detail: allowedResolutionKindsForState is a pure advisory transition table with NO principal/role/principal-kind enforcement — the package is type/data only and enforces none of CORE_INVARIANTS. Real gate authority must live in the daemon consumer. Fix: Document governance-relay as advisory; add a daemon-side test asserting a non-declared principal cannot resolve/approve a gate.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Document governance-relay as advisory; add a daemon-side test asserting a non-declared principal cannot resolve/approve a gate.

legacyRecords.title: nextRoundState is total/fail-safe (unhandled pairs no-op to current state) but diverges from allowedResolutionKindsForState (table allows take_over in 'drafting'; transition only acts on take_over from 'in_gate'), and does no authority checks
legacyRecords.detail: nextRoundState is total/fail-safe (unhandled pairs no-op to current state) but diverges from allowedResolutionKindsForState (table allows take_over in 'drafting'; transition only acts on take_over from 'in_gate'), and does no authority checks. Fix: Align transition with the table and ensure the daemon validates acting principal/role before calling it.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Align transition with the table and ensure the daemon validates acting principal/role before calling it.

legacyRecords.title: computeSha256 is correct, but the marketplace content digest is computed over BUNDLE BYTES ONLY, not the manifest — while canonical-id.ts documents digest = sha256(manifest||bundle)
legacyRecords.detail: computeSha256 is correct, but the marketplace content digest is computed over BUNDLE BYTES ONLY, not the manifest — while canonical-id.ts documents digest = sha256(manifest||bundle). The manifest (permissions[], imports[]) is stored in the DB unbound to the content address and trusted by resolve/install. So permissions/import-graph can be altered without changing the digest the daemon trusts. Fix: Make the content digest cover manifest+bundle (as canonical-id claims) or store+verify a separate manifest digest; daemon installer must verify the manifest against the address before trusting permissions/imports.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Make the content digest cover manifest+bundle (as canonical-id claims) or store+verify a separate manifest digest; daemon installer must verify the manifest against the address before trusting permissions/imports.

legacyRecords.title: parseExtensionId accepts un-namespaced ids ({namespace:'',name}); in the publish auth path an empty namespace skips the namespace→tenant ownership binding, so two tenants can both publish/overwrite the same legacy un-namespaced id (cross-tenant overwrite)
legacyRecords.detail: parseExtensionId accepts un-namespaced ids ({namespace:'',name}); in the publish auth path an empty namespace skips the namespace→tenant ownership binding, so two tenants can both publish/overwrite the same legacy un-namespaced id (cross-tenant overwrite). Regex itself is sound. Documented legacy-compat. Fix: Remove un-namespaced acceptance after migrating built-ins; meanwhile restrict empty-namespace publishes to a hard-coded legacy allowlist bound to one trusted tenant.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Remove un-namespaced acceptance after migrating built-ins; meanwhile restrict empty-namespace publishes to a hard-coded legacy allowlist bound to one trusted tenant.

legacyRecords.title: resolveClosure trusts the DB-sourced, non-integrity-bound manifest and the surfaced signature is hard-coded empty; no signature verification (relies on daemon byte-vs-digest only)
legacyRecords.detail: resolveClosure trusts the DB-sourced, non-integrity-bound manifest and the surfaced signature is hard-coded empty; no signature verification (relies on daemon byte-vs-digest only). Import digests ARE pre-validated 64-hex (safe selector). Fix: Verify manifest against content address + a real signature once available; else document resolve output as untrusted until daemon re-verifies.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Verify manifest against content address + a real signature once available; else document resolve output as untrusted until daemon re-verifies.

legacyRecords.title: resolveClosure recurses over imports with cycle detection but no depth/breadth cap; a deep/wide acyclic graph could drive large recursion/allocation on /v1/resolve
legacyRecords.detail: resolveClosure recurses over imports with cycle detection but no depth/breadth cap; a deep/wide acyclic graph could drive large recursion/allocation on /v1/resolve. Fix: Add max-node/max-depth bound and reject closures exceeding it.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Add max-node/max-depth bound and reject closures exceeding it.

legacyRecords.title: 'latest' range has no floor; a publisher able to push a high version (gated by publish authz) forces all 'latest' consumers onto it
legacyRecords.detail: 'latest' range has no floor; a publisher able to push a high version (gated by publish authz) forces all 'latest' consumers onto it. Parser rejects prereleases + malformed input (no injection). Bounded by publish authz. Fix: Pin by digest in lockfiles so a later high-version push can't silently move installed consumers.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Pin by digest in lockfiles so a later high-version push can't silently move installed consumers.

legacyRecords.title: Every resolved closure entry is emitted with hard-coded signature:'' — the consumer half of the missing-signature gap
legacyRecords.detail: Every resolved closure entry is emitted with hard-coded signature:'' — the consumer half of the missing-signature gap. The daemon installer downloads from bundleUrl with no signature to verify; authenticity rests on HTTPS-to-marketplace + digest match, no end-to-end publisher attestation. Fix: Surface revision.signature (the record field exists) and have the daemon verify against a pinned namespace key; or remove the field so consumers don't assume a guarantee that's never provided.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Surface revision.signature (the record field exists) and have the daemon verify against a pinned namespace key; or remove the field so consumers don't assume a guarantee that's never provided.

legacyRecords.title: All id fields (anchorType/anchorId/artifactId/runId) are unconstrained z.string() — empty + arbitrarily long values pass
legacyRecords.detail: All id fields (anchorType/anchorId/artifactId/runId) are unconstrained z.string() — empty + arbitrarily long values pass. Low-risk (dispatcher enforces permission + parameterized DB) but no defense-in-depth against malformed/oversized ids. Fix: z.string().min(1).max(n) + format regex where known; ensure handlers scope by ctx.tenantId regardless of supplied ids. ---
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: z.string().min(1).max(n) + format regex where known; ensure handlers scope by ctx.tenantId regardless of supplied ids. ---

legacyRecords.title: Property access cursor[segment.name] permits __proto__, constructor, prototype
legacyRecords.detail: Property access cursor[segment.name] permits __proto__, constructor, prototype. This is a read-only traversal (values read, never assigned) so it cannot pollute prototypes; impact is benign ($.__proto__ returns Object.prototype, then JSON-serialized into an artifact / matched against a failure matcher). No RCE, no pollution. - Fix (hardening): reject __proto__/constructor/prototype segment names, or guard with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(cursor, name) so special keys resolve to undefined.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: reject __proto__/constructor/prototype segment names, or guard with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(cursor, name) so special keys resolve to undefined.

legacyRecords.title: Number.parseInt allows large indices; harmless for read access (returns undefined)
legacyRecords.detail: Number.parseInt allows large indices; harmless for read access (returns undefined). No fix needed. ---
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Disposition requires current source review.

legacyRecords.title: Request URL is buildUrl(baseUrl, renderText(pathTemplate, inputs))
legacyRecords.detail: Request URL is buildUrl(baseUrl, renderText(pathTemplate, inputs)). baseUrl/pathTemplate are manifest-pinned (the contract calls this a "hard security boundary"), so host isn't directly user-controlled. But pathTemplate can embed ${ports.X.text} placeholders whose values come from upstream artifact bodies (often agent/LLM-produced), and buildUrl doesn't encode the substituted value — so //attacker/, ..%2f..%2f, or ?/# injection enables path traversal / endpoint pivoting within the pinned host and query smuggling. (Authority override is blocked because the value is appended after baseUrl.) - Fix: encodeURIComponent (strict path-segment encoder) on rendered path values before concatenation, and assert the final parsed URL's origin equals the pinned baseUrl origin.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: encodeURIComponent (strict path-segment encoder) on rendered path values before concatenation, and assert the final parsed URL's origin equals the pinned baseUrl origin.

legacyRecords.title: fetch(request.url, …) uses default redirect: "follow"
legacyRecords.detail: fetch(request.url, …) uses default redirect: "follow". A 3xx from the pinned host can redirect to an internal/metadata host (169.254.169.254, localhost) and the body is then read + extracted. - Fix: set redirect: "manual" / "error"; reject or re-validate the redirect target against an origin allowlist before following.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: set redirect: "manual" / "error"; reject or re-validate the redirect target against an origin allowlist before following.

legacyRecords.title: On HTTP ≥400 the failure summary includes truncate(response.body, 240)
legacyRecords.detail: On HTTP ≥400 the failure summary includes truncate(response.body, 240). Credentials are sent in the request, not echoed, but a misbehaving upstream could reflect a token into its error body and it would surface in the run summary. - Fix: redact known-secret substrings from summaries.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: redact known-secret substrings from summaries.

legacyRecords.title: await response.text() reads the full body with no size cap; a hostile/large response can exhaust memory
legacyRecords.detail: await response.text() reads the full body with no size cap; a hostile/large response can exhaust memory. (Request is timeout-bounded — good.) - Fix: cap body read length (stream + abort past N bytes).
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: cap body read length (stream + abort past N bytes).

legacyRecords.title: The browser telemetry API describes exporterHeaders as suitable for bearer tokens for paid drivers
legacyRecords.detail: The browser telemetry API describes exporterHeaders as suitable for bearer tokens for paid drivers. In browser code those headers are visible to users and devtools, so the API nudges callers toward exposing backend ingest secrets. Fix: Make the docs/type comment explicit that only public/proxy-scoped tokens are allowed; steer secret-bearing exporters through a server/edge gateway.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Make the docs/type comment explicit that only public/proxy-scoped tokens are allowed; steer secret-bearing exporters through a server/edge gateway.

legacyRecords.category: xss / css injection into host document
legacyRecords.title: 'style' is in ALLOWED_TAGS without allowVulnerableTags
legacyRecords.detail: 'style' is in ALLOWED_TAGS without allowVulnerableTags. sanitize-html (2.17.3) passes <style> body through UNESCAPED/UNFILTERED when allowlisted; allowedStyles only filters inline style= attrs, NOT <style> contents. This sanitized HTML is injected same-document via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (ReviewBodyRenderer.tsx:250, renderMode:'html' path — NOT the sandboxed iframe), so an untrusted extension renderer can ship global unscoped CSS reaching the RelayOS host: position:fixed full-viewport overlays (clickjacking/UI-redress of review/approve controls), @import/url() CSS exfil, host-chrome restyling. Breaks the documented renderMode:'html' guarantee (security-model.mdx:113). Fix: Remove 'style' from ALLOWED_TAGS (style via the already-url()-filtered inline style= attr). If a <style> block is truly needed, render that fragment only via the sandboxed iframe, or scope/sanitize CSS (strip @import/url()/expression, namespace selectors). Never set allowVulnerableTags.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Remove 'style' from ALLOWED_TAGS (style via the already-url()-filtered inline style= attr). If a <style> block is truly needed, render that fragment only via the sandboxed iframe, or scope/sanitize CSS (strip @import/url()/expression, namespace selectors). Never set allowVulnerableTags.

legacyRecords.title: <a target rel> allowed but rel not forced to noopener
legacyRecords.detail: <a target rel> allowed but rel not forced to noopener. Since extension-html renders same-document, <a target=_blank> without rel lets the opened page access window.opener of the host window (can navigate the host tab). javascript: already blocked, so opener abuse not script exec. Fix: transformTags on 'a' to force rel='noopener noreferrer nofollow' when target present, or drop target. ---
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: transformTags on 'a' to force rel='noopener noreferrer nofollow' when target present, or drop target. ---

legacyRecords.title: Self-update downloads the runner binary and verifies it against SHA256SUMS, but SHA256SUMS is fetched over the same TLS channel from the same host (dl.relayos.work) with NO independent/detached signature (no code-signing/Ed25519/PGP)
legacyRecords.detail: Self-update downloads the runner binary and verifies it against SHA256SUMS, but SHA256SUMS is fetched over the same TLS channel from the same host (dl.relayos.work) with NO independent/detached signature (no code-signing/Ed25519/PGP). The checksum only protects against transport corruption, not a compromised/substituted release host: anyone who can serve dl.relayos.work (host compromise, TLS MITM, DNS/CDN takeover) delivers a malicious binary + matching SHA256SUMS and it becomes the running executable → runner-host RCE. Fix: Embed a release-signing public key in the runner build; publish SHA256SUMS.sig (detached) and verify it against the pinned key before trusting the checksum; treat the download host as untrusted for integrity.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Embed a release-signing public key in the runner build; publish SHA256SUMS.sig (detached) and verify it against the pinned key before trusting the checksum; treat the download host as untrusted for integrity.

legacyRecords.title: version.json and the checksum are all rooted solely in TLS trust of dl.relayos.work with no pinning
legacyRecords.detail: version.json and the checksum are all rooted solely in TLS trust of dl.relayos.work with no pinning. Fail-closed on missing checksum (good), but the whole channel's integrity depends on TLS alone. Companion to the medium; signing the manifest closes both. Fix: Sign the version manifest + checksum; verify with a pinned key independent of TLS.
legacyRecords.recommendedFix: Sign the version manifest + checksum; verify with a pinned key independent of TLS.
